title: Objectwise comparison of cone straightening with the slice-pullback diagram
statement:
Use the marked simplicial sets, absolute model $\mathsf M$ and relative (co)cartesian models of [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model] and [lem-coef-marked-relative-cartesian-model], projective diagrams of [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus], and coherent realization and marked cone straightening of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] and [lem-coef-marked-cone-straightening-quillen]. Work in nested universes large enough for the following small constructions. For a small ordinary category $C$ and any marked simplicial set $p:X\to N(C)$, define a strict diagram $L_C(X):C\to\mathsf M$ by
$$L_C(X)(c)_r=\{(x,g):x\in X_r,\quad g:p(x_r)\to c\text{ in }C\}.$$
Here $p(x_r)$ is the image of the last vertex of $x$, and $p(x_i\to x_j)$ is the corresponding arrow in the string $p(x)$. For $\theta:[s]\to[r]$ set
$$\theta^*(x,g)=(\theta^*x,\ g\circ p(x_{\theta(s)}\to x_r)).$$
An edge $(e,g)$ is marked exactly when $e$ is marked in $X$; the action of $c\to d$ postcomposes $g$. Equivalently the underlying simplicial set is $X\times_{N(C)}N(C_{/c})$, where $C_{/c}$ has objects arrows to $c$ and morphisms their commuting triangles. Let
$$\epsilon_C:\mathfrak C[N(C)^{\mathrm{op}}]\to C^{\mathrm{op}},\qquad T_C(X)=\bigl(\operatorname{St}^+_{\epsilon_C}(X^{\mathrm{op}})\bigr)^{\mathrm{op}},$$
where $C^{\mathrm{op}}$ has discrete mapping simplicial sets and the final opposite is taken separately at every value of the $C$-diagram. Opposite of a marked simplicial set reverses vertex order and carries its marked edges to the reversed marked edges.

There is a natural transformation $a_C:T_C\to L_C$ such that for every $X$ and every $c\in C$, the map $a_{C,X}(c)$ is a weak equivalence in $\mathsf M$. No fibrancy or cofibrancy assumption on $X$ is required. For the terminal category $C=*$, the transformation $a_*$ is the natural point comparison $T_*\to\mathrm{id}$ obtained from the cone-straightening point comparison.

The transformation is natural in both $X$ and $C$: for $u:C\to D$, write $N(u)_!X$ for $X$ with base map composed with $N(u)$, and let $u_!$ denote ordinary left Kan extension of marked diagrams, characterized by $\operatorname{Nat}(u_!H,G)=\operatorname{Nat}(H,Gu)$. Under the canonical cone and slice-diagram identifications
$$u_!T_C(X)\cong T_D(N(u)_!X),\qquad u_!L_C(X)\cong L_D(N(u)_!X),$$
$u_!a_{C,X}$ agrees with $a_{D,N(u)_!X}$. These identifications and this equality respect identities and composites.
